chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'The supplication is more piercing than the spear-heads of iron.'

key_terms.أَنْفَذُ: anfadhu — comparative form of nafidh (penetrating/effective); 'more piercing/penetrating'
key_terms.الدُّعَاءُ: du'a — supplication, calling upon God; here used as the subject of comparison
key_terms.السِّنَانِ الْحَدِيدِ: al-sinan al-hadid — the iron spear-head; symbol of the sharpest and most effective physical weapon

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about the power of supplication compared to weapons?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses a vivid military metaphor to describe the power of du'a (supplication), comparing it favorably to iron spear-heads — the most penetrating weapons of his era. This teaching comes in the context of the chapter on 'supplication as the weapon of the believer,' emphasizing that spiritual means (prayer/du'a) are not merely supplementary acts but possess real, effective power exceeding that of physical force. The original audience of warriors and scholars would have understood 'more piercing than iron spear-heads' as the highest praise for effectiveness.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The supplication is more piercing than the spear-heads of the iron’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Prayer, pleading before Allah for help, is more effective than spears of iron.’”
